title: Sessions, Sandbox & Safety in Depth
description: resume/fork/archive manage the session lifecycle, while sandbox_mode, --add-dir, approval policy, and bypass modes dial autonomy from read-only up to full bypass -- gated by feature flags.

steps.content: argv = [codex, resume, --last]   (or: fork --last to branch it)
steps.annotation: resume continues a persisted session (picker by default, --last for the most recent); fork starts a new branch from a prior session instead of overwriting it.

steps.content: lifecycle: codex archive / unarchive / delete manage saved rollouts by id or name
steps.annotation: Sessions are durable records under $CODEX_HOME; archive hides one from the picker, delete removes it permanently.

steps.content: trust gate: [projects."<path>"] in config.toml marks this repo trusted -> project config may load
steps.annotation: Per-project trust decides whether a repo-local config is honored at all -- a checkout cannot grant itself privileges.

steps.content: apply the migration across the repo
steps.annotation: The task will write files, so the resolved sandbox policy decides what the shell may touch.

steps.content: resolve safety: -s read-only | workspace-write | danger-full-access ; --add-dir grants extra writable roots
steps.annotation: sandbox_mode sets the boundary; --add-dir widens it for specific directories without going full-access.

steps.content: approval: -a untrusted | on-request | never ; guardian_approval (stable/on) can escalate risky steps
steps.annotation: The approval policy is a separate dial from the sandbox: it decides when the model must ask before a command runs.

steps.content: codex sandbox -- npx prisma migrate deploy   (run inside the seatbelt sandbox)
steps.annotation: codex sandbox runs a command under the Codex-provided (seatbelt) sandbox directly -- the same isolation the loop applies to tool calls.

steps.content: migration applied; writes confined to the workspace boundary
steps.annotation: The OS-level sandbox denies out-of-bounds writes before they happen, independent of model intent.

steps.content: escape hatches: --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox (no sandbox, no prompts) and --dangerously-bypass-hook-trust -- for externally-sandboxed automation only
steps.annotation: The bypass flags remove the safety rails entirely and are meant only for environments that are already sandboxed from the outside.

steps.content: Migration applied inside the boundary; resume/fork later to continue, and features list shows which safety flags are on.
steps.annotation: Session lifecycle and the safety model are layered dials over one loop: sandbox, approval, trust, and feature flags each gate a different axis.
